title: Finance: Income, Expenditure and Budgets
summary: Types of income and expenditure, payslips and deductions, drawing up and analysing a personal or household budget, and profit and loss.

items: **Fixed income**: the same amount every month (e.g. a salary).
**Variable income**: changes from month to month (e.g. commission, tips, overtime, informal trading).
**Gross income**: total earnings before deductions. **Net income** (take-home pay): what is left after deductions.

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: **UIF** (Unemployment Insurance Fund) is 1% of gross pay, paid by the employee, and the employer pays another 1%. It provides money if you lose your job. **PAYE** is income tax deducted by the employer and paid to SARS.

items: **Fixed expenses**: stay the same each month (rent, school fees, insurance, loan repayments).
**Occasional expenses**: happen now and then (car repairs, school uniforms, gifts).

notes.text: A **budget** is a plan for income and expenditure over a period. A budget has a **surplus** if income is more than expenditure and a **deficit** if expenditure is more than income.

notes.title: Worked example 1
notes.problem: Using the budget, calculate the surplus and the percentage of income spent on rent.
notes.answer: Surplus R880; rent is about 31,9% of income

notes.caption: A negative profit is a loss

questions.memo:
(a) ✓ Expenditure R4 100 (1) ✓ Surplus R100 (1)
(b) ✓✓ A sensible suggestion, e.g. cheaper data bundle, walk/share transport, save the surplus (2)

questions.prompt: A learner makes 40 cupcakes at a total cost of R180 and sells them at R8 each. Calculate the profit if all are sold, and the minimum number she must sell to break even.
questions.memo:
✓ Income 40 × R8 = R320, profit R140 (1)
✓ Break even: R180 ÷ R8 = 22,5 (1)
✓ She must sell 23 cupcakes (1)
